body.estimand_functional: \(M_{ij}=E_P[Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]\) identifies the causal matrix and \(U=\operatorname{left}_r(M)\) is its row subspace.  The recorded estimator is \(\widehat U^{\mathrm I}=\operatorname{left}_r(\mathcal P_r(Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}))\) with \(\sup_P E_P\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)\le C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\).  The observed-data hybrid \(\widehat U^{\mathrm H}\) reports \(\widehat U^{\mathrm I}\) when \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\le1\) and the deterministic sine frame otherwise, and satisfies \(\sup_P E_P\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm H},U)\le C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\).  The causal target, the two estimators, and their risk bounds are distinct objects.

sampling_model.design: A triangular array of sequential randomized decisions ordered globally by \(o(i,j)=(i-1)m+j\), with filtration \((\mathbb G_k)_{k=0}^{nm}\) and explicit row baselines \(\mathcal F_{i,0}=\mathbb G_{(i-1)m}\).
sampling_model.units: \(n\) units observed at \(m\) ordered decision times, with bounded aspect ratio; the sharp experiment and Markov witness use \(n_\ell=2\ell\) and \(m_\ell=2\lceil\gamma\ell\rceil\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary \(A_{ij}\) is drawn with \(p_{ij}\in[q,1-q]\) given the global pre-cell field \(\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Recorded IPW--SVD uses the known predictable propensities and requires no estimated treatment nuisance.  Its expected-risk guarantee follows from bounded matrix-martingale concentration and a deterministic singular-subspace bound.  The blind procedure replaces entrywise propensities by a clipped empirical row fraction; propensity-path stability and the primitive oracle gap control its tangent expansion only at the explicit \(d_{nm}\) resolution.  The observed discrepancy compares blind and recorded fits at that same resolution and is not advertised as a \(b_{nm}\)-scale certificate.  Simultaneous bands use the direct recorded-IPW contrast and deterministic variance envelopes; leave-one-cell-out residuals and multiplier studentization are not needed for the conservative coverage theorem.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Published Theorem 1, equations (16b)--(17) on page 950, gives the rowwise upper bound, and Theorem 2, equation (22b) on page 953, gives the minimax lower bound under independent Bernoulli observation and independent noise.
Published Theorem 2.2 on page 1974 gives a Frobenius online-SGD rate and Theorem 3.1 on page 1977 gives fixed-form asymptotic normality for scalar rewards from independent Gaussian matrix contexts.
Published Theorem 3.1 and equations (17)--(18) on page 2389 bound nearest-neighbor error for each unit-by-time counterfactual mean under an adaptive pooled sequential policy.

Published Theorem 2 and equation (14) on page 1724 give a Frobenius RMSE upper bound for nuclear-norm completion of an untreated potential-outcome matrix when adoption dates are independent across units conditional on the latent matrix.

Published Theorem 3 in Section 4 of article e70002 gives a restricted-strong-convexity and Frobenius-error guarantee for the low-rank term estimated by the weighted MAR objective in equations (2) and (11).
Published Propositions 1--3 develop tall-wide factor imputation rates and limit laws for missing common components, with average and individual treatment effects on the treated as applications.

The published COLT extended abstract on pages 3821--3822 and its public full version give entrywise consistency and asymptotic normality for synthetic nearest neighbors under causal missing-not-at-random sampling.

Published Theorem 5 on page 2021 compares Frobenius upper bounds for known-propensity IPW and uniform-risk nuclear-norm completion under independent Bernoulli observation with a low-rank probability matrix.
The published article and its public full version develop groupwise nuclear-norm completion and debiased asymptotic normality for fixed block or staggered missing-not-at-random causal panels.

Public Theorem 3.2 and Corollary 3.3 give an armwise empirical-row-scaled SVD upper bound under independent Bernoulli assignments and low-rank arm means.  Only the polynomial geometry \(\sqrt{1/n+n/m^2}\) is shared: their rowwise matrix-error theorem has its own \(\log^4\) factor, whereas \(b_{nm}\) also has \(\sqrt{\log n}\) and the \(B\sqrt{nm}/\lambda_{nm}\) conversion to normalized effect-subspace loss.
Published Theorem 3 and equation (10) on page 7 characterize variance improvement for a scalar adaptively normalized IPW estimator under independent treatment indicators.
Predictably weighted adaptive IPW scores yield scalar studentized martingale limits.
Balancing weights attain Frobenius guarantees and a lower bound under fixed heterogeneous missingness.
Debiased low-rank projection yields inference for a fixed linear form under independent sampling.

ArXiv Assumption 2 on pages 7--8 gives normalized third-moment, predictable-covariance, empirical-covariance, plug-in, growth, and variance-floor conditions under which Theorem 3.3 on page 8 validates simultaneous multiplier intervals for many martingale means.
Published Theorem 4 and equation (14) on page 348 validate a multiplier maximum for a coefficient matrix under modeled nonuniform missingness.

body.tldr: Recorded propensities identify the causal effect matrix and make the IPW errors a bounded row-major martingale-difference array.  The strongest uniform same-risk statement on the frozen predictable class is now \(c b_{nm}\le\inf_{\widetilde U}\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U)]\le\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm H},U)]\le C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\), where \(\widehat U^{\mathrm H}\) is an explicit hybrid of recorded IPW--SVD and a deterministic discrete-sine frame.  Recorded IPW--SVD separately retains its \(C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) expected-risk guarantee and its estimator-specific obstruction.  Nonemptiness of the bounded-outcome class forces \(\lambda_{nm}\le2B\sqrt{nm}\); with fixed \(r,\mu,K,q\) and bounded aspect ratio this gives \(b_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n/n}\) but \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm},d_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n}\), so the available uniform stochastic resolutions do not shrink.  The minimax rate between the lower scale and a constant remains open.  Blind row scaling is certified only at \(d_{nm}\), the rank-one \(0.25/0.75\) Markov law remains a HeartSteps II stress design, and simultaneous dense-query radii retain their separate \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) factor.

project_justification.gap: Published independent-mask rowwise results do not settle causal effect-subspace risk under history-predictable assignment.  On the present bounded-outcome class a constant-propensity packing yields the lower/reference scale \(b_{nm}\), while the strongest explicit uniform upper bound is constant after hybridizing the loose IPW--SVD radius with a deterministic incoherent frame.  The accepted endogenous-target example prevents claiming \(b_{nm}\)-optimality for recorded IPW--SVD but gives no estimator-independent constant lower bound.
project_justification.niche: The contribution is an explicit same-loss minimax bracket for a causal row subspace under predictable masks, with one measurable hybrid estimator on the upper side, together with an estimator-specific IPW obstruction, a calibrated blind-normalization resolution theorem, and conservative simultaneous causal-contrast bands whose entropy cost remains separate.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the constant-propensity \(c b_{nm}\) converse, the separate \(C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) expected-risk bound for recorded IPW--SVD, and the hybrid \(C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\) upper bound.  It proves that bounded outcomes force \(\lambda_{nm}\le2B\sqrt{nm}\), exposing \(b_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n/n}\) and nonshrinking \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) and \(d_{nm}\) in the fixed-complexity bounded-aspect regime.  It retains the unconditional blind \(d_{nm}\)-resolution inequalities, the explicit Markov witness, and direct finite-sample bands with separate family-size inflation.

body.related_work:
Mehrotra, Tran, Vu, and Zampetakis are the closest rowwise estimator comparator.  Their public Algorithm 1, Theorem 3.2, and Corollary 3.3 analyze separate empirical-row-scaled SVD fits for two low-rank arm means under independent Bernoulli assignment and bound matrix-row error.  The only shared rate feature is the polynomial geometry \(\sqrt{1/n+n/m^2}\): their theorem carries its own fourth-power logarithmic factor and armwise assumptions, whereas \(b_{nm}\) additionally contains the maximum-row factor \(\sqrt{\log n}\) and the subspace conversion \(B\sqrt{nm}/\lambda_{nm}\).  No equality or transfer between the two rates is claimed.  For arbitrary arm matrices \(A_1,A_0\), the only algebraic comparison used is \(\operatorname{rank}(A_1-A_0)\le\operatorname{rank}(A_1)+\operatorname{rank}(A_0)\).  Its converse fails even with bounded entries: on a square array, a sufficiently small multiple of the identity is a bounded full-rank common component, and adding a sufficiently small rank-one effect leaves both arms full rank while their difference has rank one.  Thus effect-only low rank does not establish armwise low rank, full-class containment, or rate transfer.

Cai, Li, Chi, Poor, and Chen prove two-to-infinity upper and lower bounds for an independently sampled low-rank matrix with independent noise; those results inform the deterministic perturbation and local-packing architecture but not the predictable causal class.  Dwivedi, Tian, Tomkins, Klasnja, Murphy, and Shah bound unit-by-time counterfactual-mean error under an exogenous factor model.  Athey, Bayati, Doudchenko, Imbens, and Khosravi; Sun, Zhu, and Dubin; Bai and Ng; Agarwal, Dahleh, Shah, and Shen; Choi and Yuan; Mao, Wong, and Chen; and Wang, Wong, Mao, and Chan study other outcome-completion targets, losses, or missingness structures.  These works are informative comparators, not sources of a minimax-rate transfer to the present effect-only class.

Hadad, Hirshberg, Zhan, Wager, and Athey support the recorded-propensity martingale-score reduction, and Tropp supplies the bounded-increment matrix Freedman inequality.  Khan and Ugander analyze scalar affine normalization under independent indicators; the blind row-fraction SVD and its \(0.25/0.75\) Markov witness are new objects here and do not refute that method.  Belloni and Oliveira and Ma, Niu, Zhang, and Zhu motivate high-dimensional martingale or multiplier inference, but the retained simultaneous theorem uses finite-sample Freedman radii and a union bound.  Its \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) factor is a query-family entropy cost, not part of either subspace scale.  Spruijt-Metz et al. make saved propensities and omission sensitivity operationally relevant for the HeartSteps II consumer.

body.technical_internal_limitation: Matrix Freedman followed by a deterministic subspace inequality yields \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) for recorded IPW--SVD.  The frozen class permits future singular factors to depend on earlier outcomes, so a leave-one-row argument cannot simply treat those factors as predictable; the explicit obstruction shows this matters for that estimator.  The discrete-sine fallback limits uniform risk to a constant but does not create a shrinking estimator.  Moreover, nonemptiness forces \(\lambda_{nm}\le2B\sqrt{nm}\); at fixed \(r,\mu,K,q\) and bounded aspect ratio, this makes both \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) and the blind resolution \(d_{nm}\) at least order \(\sqrt{\log n}\).  Hence the remaining gap is between an information lower scale \(b_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n/n}\) and a constant upper bound.  No estimator-independent constant converse, shrinking uniform upper estimator, residual covariance consistency, positive random studentizer, or feasible multiplier exactness is proved.
body.honest_scope: Identification is given by the recorded IPW conditional mean.  The proved headline is the expected-risk bracket between \(c b_{nm}\) and \(C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\), with the upper endpoint attained by one explicit observed-data hybrid.  Recorded IPW--SVD separately satisfies the looser \(C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) bound.  Its endogenous-target witness refutes only uniform \(b_{nm}\)-attainment by that estimator; it does not show that every estimator measurable from \(A,Y,p\) has constant risk.  In the nonempty fixed-complexity bounded-aspect regime, the available IPW and blind stochastic resolutions are nonshrinking, so minimax contraction and the sharp constant remain open.  The blind procedure is certified only up to \(d_{nm}\); the \(0.25/0.75\) Markov sequence is its boundary example and a HeartSteps II stress design, not a refutation of a published normalization method.  Simultaneous inference uses conservative finite-sample direct-IPW radii with a separate query-family entropy factor.
